title: Role of Heat Treatment Atmosphere on the Microstructure and Surface Morphology of DLP-Fabricated High-Entropy Alloy Components.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Photocurable resin loaded with pre-alloyed FeCoCrNiMn high-entropy alloy powder used for digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing
recollection.intervention: Guess: Post-printing heat treatments at 800–1200 °C for 1–4 h under different atmospheres (argon, vacuum, nitrogen, forming gas)
recollection.structure: Guess: Fully dense FCC solid‐solution grains (~10–20 µm) with occasional oxide or nitride precipitates along grain boundaries depending on atmosphere
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Atmosphere controls surface oxidation, nitriding or decarburization during high-temperature dwell, which in turn affects grain growth, recrystallization kinetics and precipitation behavior
recollection.results: Guess: In Ar: grain size ~15 µm, microhardness ~300 HV, tensile strength ~600 MPa; in vacuum: grain size ~20 µm, ~280 HV, ~580 MPa; in N₂/forming gas: nitride formation raised hardness to ~350 HV but reduced elongation by ~10 %

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies atmosphere-dependent post-print heat treatment; its listed atmospheres, temperature range, dwell time, and alloy are incorrect. The claimed dense FCC grain structure and precipitates do not match the observed porosity, cracking, retained layering, oxides, and interparticle bonding. The mechanism mentions oxidation and kinetic effects only generically, missing the key oxygen-dependent resin gas evolution, residual carbon, oxide barriers, and densification behavior. All quantitative values and measured properties are unrelated to the reported oxygen/carbon contents, transition temperatures, and MPa-scale strengths.
